title: Minimum Time to Publish Comics
statement:
You have to publish `X` different comic books. There are `Y` printing machines and `Z` binding machines. Printing machine `i` needs `print[i]` minutes to print all pages of one comic book. Every binding machine needs `K` minutes to bind one comic book. At any point in time a machine (printing or binding) can work on at most one comic book, and a job that has started cannot be interrupted.

Each comic book is published in these steps:

1. It is put into a free printing machine `i`. After `print[i]` minutes its printed pages are taken out of the machine.
2. After a **non-negative** amount of waiting time, the printed pages are placed in a free binding machine.
3. After `K` minutes the bound book is taken out of the binding machine.

All machines are free at time `0`, and a machine can start its next job at the very moment its previous job ends. Find the minimum time at which all `X` comic books have been published.
inputFormat:
The first line contains four integers `X`, `Y`, `Z` and `K`.
The second line contains `Y` integers `print[0], print[1], ..., print[Y - 1]`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the minimum time needed to publish all `X` comic books.

examples.explanation: Print the three books on machine 0, which finishes them at times 1, 2 and 3 (machine 1 would only finish one at time 3, which is no better). With a single binder taking 4 minutes each, binding runs 1-5, 5-9 and 9-13, so everything is published at time 13.

The five earliest print completion times are 2, 4, 5 (machine 1), 6 and 8, so books become ready at those times. Three binders take the first three books and finish at 4, 6 and 7. The fourth book (ready at 6) uses the binder freed at 4 and ends at 8. The fifth (ready at 8) uses the binder freed at 6 and ends at 10.

hints: Printing and binding are two stages in a row. Think about the moments at which printed books become available to the binders.

Ready times that are as early as possible, one by one, can only help the binding stage. Which `X` print completion times (over all machines and all their jobs) are the earliest? A min-heap of each machine's next completion time gives them in order.

With sorted ready times `r[1] <= r[2] <= ...`, book `j` is bound by the binder that was freed by book `j - Z`: it finishes at `max(r[j], finish[j - Z]) + K` (just `r[j] + K` if `j <= Z`). The answer is the last finish time.
